column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give the fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) to those entitled to them; and whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

This hadith is the first of the eight hadiths that the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab (may Allah have mercy on him) added, bringing the total, with what Imam al-Nawawī (may Allah have mercy on him) collected in the Forty Hadiths, to fifty.

It is to be noted that when mentioning the imams who narrated the hadiths, the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab uses the expression kharrajahu (“recorded it”) and also rawāhu (“reported it”), while al-Nawawī's expression was rawāhu. There is no difference between the two expressions,
for their meaning is the same.

This hadith is a foundation for the division of inheritance. By al-farāʾiḍ is meant the shares fixed in the Book of Allah, which are six: two thirds, one third, one sixth, one half, one quarter and one eighth. In brief they are expressed as: two thirds, one half, and the half of each,

and the half of their halves; or: the eighth, the sixth, their doubles, and the doubles of their doubles; or: the third, the quarter, and the double and half of each. What is meant is the fixed shares, together with the inheritance without a fixed share that the Qurʾān mentions alongside them

for children inheriting together, and for siblings other than maternal half-siblings inheriting together. When children inherit together, if they are male and female, the male has the share of two females; if they are females with no male among them,

two or more have two thirds, and a single daughter has one half. This is when they are of one degree, such as daughters, or sons' daughters. If they are of two degrees and the daughters are two or more, the son's daughters get nothing,
since the daughters have taken the full two thirds. If there is one daughter, she has one half, and the son's daughter or daughters have one sixth, completing the two thirds,
because this is established in the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (reported by al-Bukhārī, 6736). If the children are males only,
whether sons or, in the absence of sons, sons' sons, one of them alone takes the whole inheritance, and several divide it equally among themselves.
What has been said about the inheritance of children is also said about the inheritance of full brothers and paternal half-brothers, with full brothers given precedence over paternal half-brothers:
males only divide the inheritance equally; if they are males and females, the male has the share of two females; a single female among them has one half, and two or more have two thirds.

Paternal half-siblings inherit as full siblings do when there are none; and if there is a full sister, she takes one half, and the paternal half-sisters with her have one sixth, completing the two thirds, whether they are one or more. As for the two parents, each of them has one sixth if the deceased has a child;
and if the child is female, the father takes the remainder as an agnatic heir (taʿṣīban). If the deceased has no child, the mother takes one third and the rest goes to the father,
except that in this case, if one of the spouses is present together with the parents, the mother takes one third of what remains after the spouse's share. These two cases are called al-ʿUmariyyatān,
because the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) ruled so.

If the deceased has brothers [or sisters], whether full, paternal or maternal, the mother's inheritance is one sixth. The grandfather, the father's father, inherits the father's inheritance in his absence; and the grandmother, in the absence of the mother, inherits one sixth,

whether she is the grandmother on the mother's side or on the father's side; when several inheriting grandmothers are together, they share the one sixth. As for maternal half-siblings, one of them inherits one sixth if the deceased has no inheriting descendant or inheriting male ascendant;

and if they are more than one—whether males only, females only, or males and females—they share one third equally, with no difference between their males and females. As for the inheritance of spouses,

the husband inherits one half if the deceased has no inheriting descendant, and if there is one, he has one quarter; the wife inherits one quarter if the deceased has no inheriting descendant, and if there is one, she has one eighth; if there is more than one wife, they share the quarter or the eighth.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has set out the division of inheritance in His Mighty Book in three verses. The first verse is the words of the Exalted: “Allah instructs you concerning your children…” [al-Nisāʾ 4:11], to the end of the verse; it concerns the inheritance of the two direct lines of lineage, the deceased's ascendants and descendants. The second verse is His words:

“And for you is half of what your wives leave…” [al-Nisāʾ 4:12], to the end of the verse; it concerns the inheritance of spouses and maternal half-siblings. The third verse is the words of the Exalted in the last verse of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: “They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah…” [al-Nisāʾ 4:176], to the end of the verse; it concerns the inheritance of full siblings and paternal half-siblings.

From the above it is clear that sons and sons' sons, however far down, when there are females with them, share the inheritance, the male having the share of two females; likewise full brothers and paternal half-brothers share it with their sisters, the male having the share of two females.

As for the sons of maternal half-brothers, they have no share in the inheritance. As for the sons of full brothers and of paternal half-brothers, and likewise paternal uncles, however far up, and the sons of paternal uncles, however far down, their males take the inheritance to the exclusion of their sisters,
because no fixed share is assigned to their females when they are alone, so likewise they have no inheritance when they are together [with the males], and the males among them alone inherit,
because he ﷺ said: “Give the fixed shares to those entitled to them; and whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative.”
If the deceased has a daughter or daughters, a full sister or full sisters, and also paternal half-brothers, the paternal half-brothers do not inherit,
and the full sister or sisters inherit what exceeds the daughters' share as agnatic heirs together with another (taʿṣīban maʿa al-ghayr),

because this is established in the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (reported by al-Bukhārī, 6741 and 6742). This is thus an exception to the hadith, “Give the fixed shares to those entitled to them; and whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative”,
because full sisters are closer to the deceased than paternal half-brothers.
The point of mentioning “male” (dhakar) after “man” (rajul) in his words, “to the nearest male relative (li-awlā rajulin dhakar)”, is that a rajul is one who is grown and has vigour and strength;
so the word “male” was added to make clear that inheritance depends on maleness, not on manhood and strength, so the very old and the very young are equal in it.
The Sharīʿah is perfect and contains general, universal principles, as this hadith shows.
Those who inherit by fixed share are given precedence and receive their inheritance, and what remains goes to those who inherit without a fixed amount.
On the basis of this hadith, the preponderant view on the question of the grandfather and the brothers is that the grandfather alone inherits, to the exclusion of the brothers,

because he is an ascendant, while the brothers inherit as kalālah; the grandfather is like the father and takes the inheritance without them. Likewise, the preponderant view is to give precedence to maternal half-brothers over full brothers in the case of al-musharrakah,

because maternal half-brothers inherit by fixed share and full brothers inherit as agnatic heirs; the holder of a fixed share is given his share, and those who inherit as agnatic heirs take what remains if anything remains after the fixed shares, and otherwise they are excluded.
